creator: N.S. Mankoč Borštnik
description: Abstract Using the odd and even “basis vectors”, which are the superposition of odd and even products of γ a \gamma^{a} ’s, to describe the internal spaces of the second quantised fermion and boson fields, respectively, offers in even-dimensional spaces, like it is d = ( 13 + 1 ) d=(13+1) , the unique description of all the properties of

title: ConceptPose: Training-Free Zero-Shot Object Pose Estimation using Concept Vectors
creator: Liming Kuang, Yordanka Velikova, Mahdi Saleh, Jan-Nico Zaech, Danda Pani Paudel, Benjamin Busam
description: Abstract Object pose estimation is a fundamental task in computer vision and robotics, yet most methods require extensive, dataset-specific training. Concurrently, large-scale vision language models show remarkable zero-shot capabilities. In this work, we bridge these two worlds by introducing ConceptPose, a framework for object pose estimation that is both training-free and model-free.

title: Conserved Pseudomomenta in Linear Quasigeostrophic Fluid Flows From Noether’s Theorem
creator: Dušan Beguš, Chenyu Zhang, J. B. Marston
description: Abstract Hamiltonian and Lagrangian formulations for the two-dimensional quasi-geostrophic equations linearized about a zonally-symmetric basic flow are presented. The Lagrangian and Hamiltonian exhibit an infinite U(1) symmetry due to the absence of wave + wave → \rightarrow wave interactions in the linearized approximation.

title: A Diffusion-Based Framework for High-Resolution Precipitation Forecasting over CONUS
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . Accurate precipitation forecasting is essential for hydrometeorological risk management, especially for anticipating extreme rainfall that can lead to flash flooding and infrastructure damage. This study introduces a diffusion-based deep learning (DL) framework that systematically compares three residual prediction strategies differing only in their input sources: (1) a fully data-driven model using only past observations from the Multi-Radar Multi-Sensor (MRMS) system, (2) a corrective model using only forecasts from the High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) numerical weather prediction system, and (3) a hybrid model integrating

title: Unsupervised Kinematic Dissection of the Solar Neighborhood: Identifying Stellar Moving Groups with Gaia DR3
creator: Anmay Raj
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anmay Raj. We present a comprehensive kinematic analysis of the solar neighborhood ( d < 50 d<50 pc) using high-precision astrometric data from the third Gaia Data Release (DR3). By leveraging the full six-dimensional phase space information (positions and velocities), we apply the Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm to blindly identify stellar overdensities in the Galactocentric Cartesian velocity space ( U , V , W U,V,W ).

title: Contrast transfer functions help quantify neural network out-of-distribution generalization in HRTEM
creator: Luis Rangel DaCosta \ORCID 0000-0001-8966-0408, Mary C. Scott \ORCID 0000-0002-9543-6725
description: Abstract Neural networks, while effective for tackling many challenging scientific tasks, are not known to perform well out-of-distribution (OOD), i.e., within domains which differ from their training data. Understanding neural network OOD generalization is paramount to their successful deployment in experimental workflows, especially when ground-truth knowledge about the experiment is hard to establish or experimental conditions significantly vary.

title: ORCA: Open-ended Response Correctness Assessment for Audio Question Answering
creator: Šimon Sedláček, Sara Barahona, Bolaji Yusuf, Laura Herrera-Alarcón, Santosh Kesiraju, Cecilia Bolaños, Alicia Lozano-Diez, Sathvik Udupa, Fernando López, Allison Ferner, Ramani Duraiswami, Jan Černocký
description: Abstract Evaluating open-ended responses from large audio language models (LALMs) is challenging because human annotators often genuinely disagree on answer correctness due to multiple valid interpretations, partial correctness, and subjective judgment. Traditional metrics reporting only mean scores fail to capture this uncertainty.

title: Causal Attribution of Model Performance Gaps in Medical Imaging Under Distribution Shifts
creator: Pedro M. Gordaliza, Nataliia Molchanova, Jaume Banus, Thomas Sanchez, Meritxell Bach Cuadra, [2mm] CIBM Center for Biomedical Imaging
description: Abstract Deep learning models for medical image segmentation suffer significant performance drops due to distribution shifts, but the causal mechanisms behind these drops remain poorly understood. We extend causal attribution frameworks to high-dimensional segmentation tasks, quantifying how acquisition protocols and annotation variability independently contribute to performance degradation.

title: Relic Density Topology as a Discriminatory Tool: A Comparative Analysis of IDM, MSSM, and NMSSM Dark Matter
creator: Mohid Farhan
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohid Farhan. This study proposes a diagnostic mechanism based on the relic density topology to discriminate between the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM), and the Next-to-Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (NMSSM). Using a unified numerical scan with micrOMEGAs over the heavy-mass regime ( m χ > 300 ​ GeV m_{\chi}>300~\text{GeV} ), we contrast the phenomenological profiles of these frameworks.

title: Food Image Generation on Multi-Noun Categories
creator: Xinyue PanPurdue University pan161@purdue.edu, Yuhao Chen University of Waterloo yuhao.chen1@uwaterloo.ca Jiangpeng HePurdue University he416@purdue.edu Fengqing ZhuPurdue University zhu0@purdue.edu
description: Abstract Generating realistic food images for categories with multiple nouns is surprisingly challenging. For instance, the prompt “egg noodle” may result in images that incorrectly contain both eggs and noodles as separate entities. Multi-noun food categories are common in real-world datasets and account for a large portion of entries in benchmarks such as UEC-256.

title: Cognitive Trust in HRI: “Pay Attention to Me and I’ll Trust You Even if You are Wrong” Proceedings of the 2026 ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction (HRI ’26), March 16–19, 2026, Edinburgh, Scotland, UK CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in HCI
creator: Adi Manor, Dan Cohen, Ziv Keidar, Avi Parush, Hadas Erel
description: Abstract . Cognitive trust and the belief that a robot is capable of accurately performing tasks, are recognized as central factors in fostering high-quality human-robot interactions. It is well established that performance factors such as the robot’s competence and its reliability shape cognitive trust.

title: Explaining the Unseen: Multimodal Vision-Language Reasoning for Situational Awareness in Underground Mining Disasters
creator: Mizanur Rahman Jewel, Mohamed Elmahallawy, Sanjay Madria, Samuel Frimpong
description: Abstract Underground mining disasters produce pervasive darkness, dust, and collapses that obscure vision and make situational awareness difficult for humans and conventional systems. To address this, we propose MDSE , Multimodal Disaster Situation Explainer, a novel vision-language framework that automatically generates detailed textual explanations of post-disaster underground scenes.

title: AgentComp: From Agentic Reasoning to Compositional Mastery in Text-to-Image Models
creator: Arman Zarei, Jiacheng Pan, Matthew Gwilliam, Soheil Feizi, Zhenheng Yang
description: Abstract Text-to-image generative models have achieved remarkable visual quality but still struggle with compositionality—accurately capturing object relationships, attribute bindings, and fine-grained details in prompts. A key limitation is that models are not explicitly trained to differentiate between compositionally similar prompts and images, resulting in outputs that are close to the intended description yet deviate in fine-grained details.

title: Modular Deep-Learning-Based Early Warning System for Deadly Heatwave Prediction
creator: Shangqing Xu, Zhiyuan Zhao, Megha Sharma, José María Martín-Olalla, Alexander Rodríguez, Gregory A. Wellenius, B. Aditya Prakash
description: Abstract Severe heatwaves in urban areas significantly threaten public health, calling for establishing early warning strategies. Despite predicting occurrence of heatwaves and attributing historical mortality, predicting an incoming deadly heatwave remains a challenge due to the difficulty in defining and estimating heat-related mortality.

title: High deuteration of methanol in L1544 Based on observations carried out with the IRAM 30 m telescope. IRAM is supported by INSU/CNRS (France), MPG (Germany), and IGN (Spain).
creator: Silvia Spezzano 1, Wiebke Riedel 1, Paola Caselli 1, Olli Sipilä 1, Yuxin Lin 1, Hayley A. Bunn 1, Elena Redaelli 2, Laurent H. Coudert 3, Andrés Megías 4, Izaskun Jimenez-Serra 4
description: Abstract Isotopic fractionation is a very powerful tool to follow the evolution of material from one stage to the next in the star-formation process. Pre-stellar cores exhibit some of the highest levels of deuteration because their physical conditions (T ≤ \leq 10 K and n n (H 2 ) ≥ \geq 10 5 cm -3 ) greatly favor deuteration processes.

title: Masked Generative Policy for Robotic Control
creator: Lipeng Zhuang Shiyu Fan Florent P. Audonnet Yingdong Ru Gerardo Aragon Camarasa Paul Henderson University of Glasgow, Glasgow, United Kingdom
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lipeng Zhuang Shiyu Fan Florent P. Audonnet Yingdong Ru Gerardo Aragon Camarasa Paul Henderson University of Glasgow, Glasgow, United Kingdom. We present Masked Generative Policy (MGP), a novel framework for visuomotor imitation learning. We represent actions as discrete tokens, and train a conditional masked transformer that generates tokens in parallel and then rapidly refines only low-confidence tokens.

title: SuperF: Neural Implicit Fields for Multi-Image Super-Resolution
creator: Sander Riisøen Jyhne, Christian Igel, Morten Goodwin, Per-Arne Andersen, Serge Belongie, Nico Lang
description: Abstract High-resolution imagery is often hindered by limitations in sensor technology, atmospheric conditions, and costs. Such challenges occur in satellite remote sensing, but also with handheld cameras, such as our smartphones. Hence, super-resolution aims to enhance the image resolution algorithmically. Since single-image super-resolution requires solving an inverse problem, such methods must exploit strong priors, e.g.

title: On Event-Triggered Extremum Seeking via Standard and Lie-Bracket Averaging: A Hybrid Dynamical Systems Approach
creator: Mahmoud Abdelgalil, Jorge I. Poveda
description: Abstract We introduce and analyze the stability of a class of event-triggered extremum-seeking algorithms designed to solve resource-aware, model-free, optimization problems. Leveraging recent advances in Lie-Bracket Averaging for hybrid systems, we demonstrate that the proposed controllers can be formulated as well-posed multi-time-scale hybrid systems that satisfy key regularity, stability, and robustness properties.

title: Mental Models of Autonomy and Sentience Shape Reactions to AI CCS: Human-centered computing HCI theory, concepts and models CCS: Human-centered computing Collaborative and social computing theory, concepts and paradigms CCS: Computing methodologies Theory of mind CCS: Applied computing Psychology CC
creator: Janet V. T. Pauketat, Daniel B. Shank, Aikaterina Manoli, Jacy Reese Anthis
description: Abstract . Abstract Narratives about artificial intelligence (AI) entangle autonomy, the capacity to self-govern, with sentience, the capacity to sense and feel. AI agents that perform tasks autonomously and companions that recognize and express emotions may activate mental models of autonomy and sentience, respectively, provoking distinct reactions.

title: Islands of Instability in Nonlinear Wavefunction Models in the Continuum: A Different Route to “Chaos”
creator: W. David Wick
description: Abstract Abstract In two previous papers the author described “Islands of Instability” that may appear in wavefunction models with nonlinear evolution (of a type proposed originally in the context of the Measurement Problem). Such “IsoI” represent a new scenario for Hamiltonian systems implying so-called “chaos”.

title: Learning Unmasking Policies for Diffusion Language Models
creator: Metod Jazbec, Theo X. Olausson, Louis Béthune, Pierre Ablin, Michael Kirchhof, João Monteiro, Victor Turrisi, Jason Ramapuram, Marco Cuturi
description: Abstract Diffusion (Large) Language Models (dLLMs) now match the downstream performance of their autoregressive counterparts on many tasks, while holding the promise of being more efficient during inference. One particularly successful variant is masked discrete diffusion, in which a buffer filled with special mask tokens is progressively replaced with tokens sampled from the model’s vocabulary.

title: Bayesian Optimization of Laser-Wakefield Acceleration via Spectral Pulse Shaping
creator: B. Z. Djordjević, C. Benedetti, A. D. McNaughton, R. Lehe, H.-E. Tsai, S. C. Wilks, B. A. Reagan, G. J. Williams, J. van Tilborg, C. B. Schroeder
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by B. Z. Djordjević, C. Benedetti, A. D. McNaughton, R. Lehe, H.-E. Tsai, S. C. Wilks, B. A. Reagan, G. J. Williams, J. van Tilborg, C. B. Schroeder. In this paper, we investigate the effect of spectral pulse shaping of the laser driver on the performance of channel-guided, laser-plasma accelerators. The study was carried out with the assistance of Bayesian optimization using particle-in-cell simulations.

title: Complementary strengths of the Neyman-Rubin and graphical causal frameworks
creator: Tetiana Gorbach
description: Abstract This article contributes to the discussion on the relationship between the Neyman-Rubin and the graphical frameworks for causal inference. We present specific examples of data-generating mechanisms — such as those involving undirected or deterministic relationships and cycles — where analyses using a directed acyclic graph are challenging, but where the tools from the Neyman-Rubin causal framework are readily applicable.

title: A novel two loop inverse seesaw model
creator: Gonzalo Benítez-Irarrázabal, Rocío Branada Balbontín, Cesar Bonilla, A. E. Cárcamo Hernández, Sergey Kovalenko, Juan Marchant González
description: Abstract We propose a Standard Model (SM) extension where neutrinos get masses through a two-loop inverse seesaw mechanism. This naturally explains the smallness of the neutrino masses and allows seesaw mediators to be at the TeV scale with testable phenomenology. The model adds two real singlet scalars and four electrically neutral leptons to the SM.

title: Gate-Tunable Superconducting Spin Valve in a van der Waals Ferromagnet/Superconductor/Ferromagnet Trilayer
creator: A. S. Ianovskaia, G. A. Bobkov, A. M. Bobkov, I.V. Bobkova
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by A. S. Ianovskaia, G. A. Bobkov, A. M. Bobkov, I.V. Bobkova. We theoretically demonstrate a gate-tunable superconducting spin valve effect (SVE) in a van der Waals (vdW) heterostructure composed of a monolayer superconductor (S) sandwiched between two ferromagnetic (F) monolayers (F/S/F). By electrostatically gating the ferromagnetic layers to modulate their chemical potentials, the system can be continuously tuned between the standard , inverse and triplet (non-monotonic) SVE regimes within the same device.

title: Metrics for Optimizing Searches for Orbital Precession and Tidal Decay via Transit- and Occultation-Timing Journal: AJ astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , numpy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , scipy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) , astr
creator: Brian Jackson, Elisabeth R. Adams, Rachel M. Huchmala, Malia Barker, Marvin Rothmeier, Jeffrey P. Morgenthaler, Amanda A. Sickafoose
description: Abstract Short-period exoplanets may exhibit orbital precession driven by several different processes, including tidal interactions with their host stars and secular interactions with additional planets. This motion manifests as periodic shifts in the timing between transits which may be detectable via high-precision and long-baseline transit- and occultation-timing measurements.

title: A Categorical Analysis of Large Language Models and Why LLMs Circumvent the Symbol Grounding Problem
creator: Luciano Floridi 1,2,* , Yiyang Jia 3,* , Fernando Tohmé 4,5
description: Abstract This paper presents a formal, categorical framework for analysing how humans and large language models (LLMs) transform content into truth-evaluated propositions about a state space of possible worlds W W , in order to argue that LLMs do not solve but circumvent the symbol grounding problem.

title: On the connection between galaxy orientation and halo absorption properties Corresponding authors: Rohan Venkat and Hsiao-Wen Chen
creator: Rohan Venkat 1, Soo May Wee 1, Hsiao-Wen Chen 2,3
description: Abstract We present a systematic investigation of the azimuthal dependence of metal-line absorption in the circumgalactic medium (CGM) using a uniformly selected sample of 87 isolated galaxies at z < 0.4 z<0.4 from the Magellan MagE Mg 2 (M3) halo survey.

title: Enhanced Squeezing and Faster Metrology from Layered Quantum Neural Networks
creator: Nickholas Gutierrez, Rodrigo Araiza Bravo, Susanne Yelin
description: Abstract Spin squeezing is a powerful resource for quantum metrology, and recent hardware platforms based on interacting qubits provide multiple possible architectures to generate and reverse squeezing during a sensing protocol. In this work, we compare the sensing performance of three such architectures—quantum reservoir computers (QRCs), quantum perceptrons, and multi-layer quantum neural networks (QNNs)—when used as squeezing-based field sensors.

title: Binding Kinetics Oppositely Regulates type II Topoisomerase Relaxation and Decatenation Activities
creator: Cleis Battaglia, Filippo Conforto, Yair Augusto Gutiérrez Fosado, Matt Newton, Erin Cutts, Davide Michieletto, Antonio Valdés
description: Abstract Type II Topoisomerases (topo II) are critical to simplify genome topology during transcription and replication. They identify topological problems and resolve them by passing a double-stranded DNA segment through a transient break in another segment. The precise mechanisms underpinning topo IIs ability to maintain a topologically simple genome are not fully understood.

title: GEOMETRIC INVARIANTS AND THE MONGE-AMPÈRE EQUATION IN KÄHLER GEOMETRY Thanks: Work supported in part by the National Science Foundation under grants DMS-22-03273, DMS-25-05241, and DMS-23-03508, and the collaboration grant 946730 from Simons Foundation.
creator: Bin Guo and Duong H. Phong
description: Abstract . This is a contribution to the special issue of Surveys in Differential Geometry celebrating the 75th birthday of Shing-Tung Yau. The bulk of the paper is devoted to a survey of some new geometric inequalities and estimates for the Monge-Ampère equation, obtained by the authors in the last few years in joint work with F. Tong, J.

title: System Energies for Pentaquark Family Using Thomas-Fermi Quark Model Journal: Annals of Physics
creator: Suman Baral, Bipin Aryal, Mohan Giri, Artem Denisenko, Gopi Chandra Kaphle, Walter Wilcox
description: Abstract This study calculates the system energies of families of pentaquarks, u ​ u ​ d ​ c ​ c ¯ uudc\overline{c} , starting from 5 quarks up to 70 using Thomas-Fermi statistical quark model. The model assumes spherical symmetry with the particles continuously distributed with varying densities and boundaries.

title: Transport Scaling and Critical Tilt Effects in Disordered 2D Dirac Fermions
creator: Swadeepan Nanda, Pavan Hosur
description: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) Dirac fermions occur ubiquitously in condensed matter systems from topological phases to quantum critical points. Since the advent of topological semimetals, where the dispersion is often tilted around the band crossing where the Dirac fermion can appear, tilt has emerged as a key handle that controls physical properties.

title: Local Banach Space Theoretic Approach to Bohr’s Theorem for Vector Valued Holomorphic and Pluriharmonic Functions
creator: Himadri Halder
description: Abstract . We study Bohr’s theorem for vector valued holomorphic and operator valued pluriharmonic functions on complete Reinhardt domains in ℂ n \mathbb{C}^{n} . Using invariants from local Banach space theory, we show that the associated Bohr radius is always strictly positive and obtain its asymptotic behavior separately in the finite- and infinite-dimensional settings.

title: Riemannian vs. Euclidean Representation of Gait Kinematics: A Comparative Analysis
creator: Tomáš Bůžek
description: Abstract Accurate quantification of complex human movements, such as gait, is essential for clinical diagnosis and rehabilitation but is often limited by traditional linear models rooted in Euclidean geometry. These frameworks frequently fail to capture the intrinsic non-linear dynamics and posture-dependent dependencies of biological systems.

title: Inhomogeneous Branching Random Walks: Incorporating Genealogy and Density Effects
creator: L. Ajax, B. Durham, P. Hebbar, C. Johnson, J. Zhang
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by L. Ajax, B. Durham, P. Hebbar, C. Johnson, J. Zhang. In this paper, we introduce a novel framework using inhomogeneous Branching Random Walks (BRWs) to model growth processes, specifically introducing genealogy-dependence in branching rates and displacement distributions to model phenomena like bacterial colony growth. Current stochastic models often either assume independent and identical behavior of individual agents or incorporate only spatiotemporal inhomogeneity, ignoring the effect of genealogy-based inhomogeneity on the long-time behavior of these processes.

title: PILLTOP: Multi-Material Topology Optimization of Polypills for Prescribed Drug-Release Kinetics Journal: Computer-Aided Design
creator: Rahul Kumar Padhy, Aaditya Chandrasekhar, Amir M. Mirzendehdel
description: Abstract Polypills are single oral dosage forms that combine multiple active pharmaceutical ingredients and excipients, enabling fixed-dose combination therapies, coordinated multi-phase release, and precise customization of patient-specific treatment protocols. Recent advances in additive manufacturing facilitate the physical realization of multi-material excipients, offering superior customization of target release profiles.

title: MindShift: Analyzing Language Models’ Reactions to Psychological Prompts
creator: Anton Vasiliuk, Irina Abdullaeva, Polina Druzhinina, Anton Razzhigaev, Andrey Kuznetsov
description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) hold the potential to absorb and reflect personality traits and attitudes specified by users. In our study, we investigated this potential using robust psychometric measures. We adapted the most studied test in psychological literature, namely Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory (MMPI) and examined LLMs’ behavior to identify traits.

title: Tidal disruption event Calorimetry: Observational constraints on the physics of TDE optical flares
creator: A. Mummery, B. D. Metzger, S. van Velzen, M. Guolo
description: Abstract Tidal disruption events are routinely discovered as bright optical/UV flares, the properties of which are now well categorized on the population level. The underlying physical processes that produce the evolution of their X-ray emission and their long-lasting UV/optical plateau are well understood; however, the origin of their early-time optical/UV emission remains the subject of much debate and uncertainty.

title: AI-Driven Expansion and Application of the Alexandria Database
creator: Théo Cavignac, Jonathan Schmidt, Pierre-Paul De Breuck, Antoine Loew, Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Hai-Chen Wang, Anton Bochkarev, Yury Lysogorskiy, Aldo H. Romero, Ralf Drautz, Silvana Botti, Miguel A. L. Marques
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Théo Cavignac, Jonathan Schmidt, Pierre-Paul De Breuck, Antoine Loew, Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Hai-Chen Wang, Anton Bochkarev, Yury Lysogorskiy, Aldo H. Romero, Ralf Drautz, Silvana Botti, Miguel A. L. Marques. We present a novel multi-stage workflow for computational materials discovery that achieves a 99% success rate in identifying compounds within 100 meV/atom of thermodynamic stability, with a threefold improvement over previous approaches.

title: Skin_Effects_in_Magnetic_Turbulence_Diffusion
creator: nick.emelyanov2014
description: Abstract The influence of electromagnetic skin effect on anomalous charged particle transport in dense, non-relativistic, collisionless plasma with a small-scale turbulent magnetic field was investigated using quasi-linear kinetic equations, through both analytical and numerical methods. Analytical expressions for the diffusion tensor components in the Fokker–Planck equation that take this effect into account have been found.

title: Understanding the Failure Modes of Transformers through the Lens of Graph Neural Networks
creator: Hunjae Lee
description: Abstract Transformers and more specifically decoder-only transformers dominate modern LLM architectures. While they have shown to work exceptionally well, they are not without issues, resulting in surprising failure modes and predictably asymmetric performance degradation. This article is a study of many of these observed failure modes of transformers through the lens of graph neural network (GNN) theory.

title: WOLF: Werewolf-based Observations for LLM Deception and Falsehoods
creator: Mrinal Agarwal, Saad Rana, Theo Sundoro, Hermela Berhe, Spencer Kim, Vasu Sharma, Sean O’Brien, Kevin Zhu
description: Abstract Deception is a fundamental challenge for multi-agent reasoning: effective systems must strategically conceal information while detecting misleading behavior in others. Yet most evaluations reduce deception to static classification, ignoring the interactive, adversarial, and longitudinal nature of real deceptive dynamics. Large language models (LLMs) can deceive convincingly but remain weak at detecting deception in peers.

title: TiNy Titans HI: Discovering Satellites via HI Gas in an Isolated, Compact Group of Dwarf Galaxies CASA (CASA Team et al. 2022), DRAGONS (Labrie et al. 2023), CARTA (doi:105281/zenodo.3377984)
creator: Sabrina Stierwalt, Nicholas Luber, Zelie Goldberg Little, George C. Privon, Gurtina Besla, Kelsey E. Johnson, Nitya Kallivayalil, David R. Patton, Mary Putman, David Simpson Heil
description: Abstract We report on the HI content of an isolated, compact group of 6 dwarf galaxies at a distance of 145 Mpc. The distribution and kinematics of the HI, including multiple gaseous bridges, indicate the group is a gravitationally bound system.

title: GTAvatar: Bridging Gaussian Splatting and Texture Mapping for Relightable and Editable Gaussian Avatars
creator: Kelian Baert Mae Younes Francois Bourel Marc Christie Adnane Boukhayma Univ Rennes, Inria, CNRS, IRISA, France
description: Abstract Recent advancements in Gaussian Splatting have enabled increasingly accurate reconstruction of photorealistic head avatars, opening the door to numerous applications in visual effects, videoconferencing, and virtual reality. This, however, comes with the lack of intuitive editability offered by traditional triangle mesh–based methods.

title: Finite V 2 ​ Δ V_{\rm 2\Delta} puzzle in low-multiplicity pp collisions from ultra-long-range azimuthal correlations in the string-shoving model
creator: Antonio Ortiz, Dushmanta Sahu, Gyula Bencedi
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Antonio Ortiz, Dushmanta Sahu, Gyula Bencedi. Ultra-long range angular correlations have been recently reported by the ALICE collaboration in pp collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV below d ​ N ch / d ​ η = 7 {\rm d}N_{\rm ch}/{\rm d}\eta=7 . The measurements have been performed as a function of the charged-particle multiplicity at midrapidity ( N ch N_{\rm ch} in | η | < 0.8 |\eta|<0.8 ), which is known to be strongly sensitive to local multiplicity fluctuations.

title: Deep Learning Surrogates for Gas Dynamics: A Physics-Informed Pedagogical Approach
creator: Ehsan Roohi
description: Abstract Compressible flow problems are characterized by highly nonlinear, implicit, and often transcendental governing equations. In undergraduate gas dynamics education, solving these equations traditionally relies on iterative numerical methods or extensive look-up tables, which can obscure the physical intuition of the solution space.

title: LLMs for Analog Circuit Design Continuum (ACDC)
creator: Yasaman Esfandiari, Jocelyn Rego, Austin Meyer, Jonathan Gallagher, Mia Levy
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yasaman Esfandiari, Jocelyn Rego, Austin Meyer, Jonathan Gallagher, Mia Levy. Large Language Models (LLMs) and transformer architectures have shown impressive reasoning and generation capabilities across diverse natural language tasks. However, their reliability and robustness in real-world engineering domains remain largely unexplored, limiting their practical utility in human-centric workflows. In this work, we investigate the applicability and consistency of LLMs for analog circuit design—a task requiring domain-specific reasoning, adherence to physical constraints, and representations—focusing on AI-assisted design where humans remain in the loop.

title: Residual Primitive Fitting of 3D Shapes with SuperFrusta
creator: Aditya Ganeshan, Matheus Gadelha, Thibault Groueix, Zhiqin Chen, Vladimir Kim, Wang Yifan, Daniel Ritchie, Adobe Research
description: Abstract We introduce a framework for converting 3D shapes into compact and editable assemblies of analytic primitives, directly addressing the persistent trade-off between reconstruction fidelity and parsimony. Our approach combines two key contributions: a novel primitive, termed SuperFrustum, and an iterative fitting algorithm, Residual Primitive Fitting (ResFit).

title: Aerodynamic Forces on a Wing Surfing in a Two-dimensional Vortex Wake
creator: Siyang Hao, Kenneth Breuer 1
description: Abstract Inspired by the wake-surfing nature of animals, this study aims to understand the aerodynamic force variation on a wing surfing in an unsteady 2-D wake. Wind tunnel experiments were conducted using Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) and force measurements with a fixed wing immersed in the wake of a pitching airfoil.

title: Tightness and solidity in fragments of Peano Arithmetic
creator: Piotr Gruza , Leszek Aleksander Kołodziejczyk and Mateusz Łełyk
description: Abstract It was shown by Visser that Peano Arithmetic has the property that any two bi-interpretable extensions of it (in the same language) are equivalent. Enayat proposed to refer to this property of a theory as tightness and to carry out a more systematic study of tightness and its stronger variants that he called neatness and solidity.

title: Exact and Efficient Stabilizer Simulation of Thermal-Relaxation Noise for Quantum Error Correction
creator: Sean R. Garner, Nathan M. Myers, Meng Wang, Samuel Stein, Chenxu Liu, Ang Li
description: Abstract Stabilizer-based simulation of quantum error-correcting codes typically relies on the Pauli-twirling approximation (PTA) to render non-Clifford noise classically tractable, but PTA can distort the behavior of physically relevant channels such as thermal relaxation. Physically accurate noise simulation is needed to train decoders and understand the noise suppression capabilities of quantum error correction codes.

title: iSTARMOD : a Python Code to Quantify Chromospheric Activity by Using the Spectral Subtraction Technique Journal: AJ Facilities: CAO:2.2m (FOCES),CAO:3.5m (CARMENES) ARES is available at this webpage: https://github.com/sousasag/ARES . Astropy ( 3 ) is available at GitHub: https://github.com/astropy/
creator: Fernando Labarga, David Montes
description: Abstract The use of the spectral subtraction technique allows measurements of chromospheric activity in late-type stars across several activity indicators, such as H α \alpha and the other Balmer lines in the visible, He i D 3 and Na i D 1 {}_{\text{1}} , D 2 {}_{\text{2}} , Ca ii H and K, and Ca ii infrared triplet, as well

title: Towards Optimal Valve Prescription for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) Surgery: A Machine Learning Approach
creator: Phevos Paschalidis, Vasiliki Stoumpou, Lisa Everest, Yu Ma, Talhat Azemi, Jawad Haider, Steven Zweibel, Eleftherios M. Protopapas, Jeff Mather, Maciej Tysarowski, George E. Sarris, Robert C. Hagberg, Howard L. Haronian, Dimitris Bertsimas
description: Abstract Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) has emerged as a prominent, minimally invasive treatment for patients with severe aortic stenosis, a life-threatening cardiovascular condition. Multiple transcatheter heart valves (THV) have been approved for use in TAVR, but current guidelines regarding valve type prescription remain a topic of ongoing debate within the medical community.

title: Predictive Compressibility Transformation for Hypersonic Turbulent Boundary Layers with Cold Walls
creator: Engin Danis
description: Abstract Compressibility transformations are widely used to relate hypersonic zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers to incompressible reference states, but their assessment has largely focused on the apparent collapse of transformed mean velocity profiles, without enforcing a unique, Mach-independent representation of the mean shear.

title: Tensor-Compressed and Fully-Quantized Training of Neural PDE Solvers
creator: Jinming Lu, Jiayi Tian, Yequan Zhao, Hai Li, Zheng Zhang
description: Abstract Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) by embedding physical laws into neural network training objectives. However, their deployment on resource-constrained platforms is hindered by substantial computational and memory overhead, primarily stemming from higher-order automatic differentiation, intensive tensor operations, and reliance on full-precision arithmetic.

title: IntegralGP: Volumetric estimation of subterranean geochemical properties in mineral deposits by fusing assay data with different spatial supports
creator: Anna Chlingaryan, Arman Melkumyan, Raymond Leung † {\dagger} School of Life and Environmental Sciences, Faculty of Science ⋆ \star Rio Tinto Sydney Innovation Hub, Faculty of EngineeringThe University of Sydney
description: Abstract This article presents an Integral Gaussian Process (IntegralGP) framework for volumetric estimation of subterranean properties in mineral deposits. It provides a unified representation for data with different spatial supports, which enables blasthole geochemical assays to be properly modelled as interval observations rather than points. This approach is shown to improve regression performance and boundary delineation.

title: Optimal Screening in Experiments with Partial Compliance Thanks: We thank Peter Hull and seminar participants at the 2025 STEP UP Conference at UNSW for helpful comments.
creator: Christopher Carter Adeline Delavande Mario Fiorini Peter Siminski Patrick Vu
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Christopher Carter Adeline Delavande Mario Fiorini Peter Siminski Patrick Vu. This note studies optimal experimental design under partial compliance when experimenters can screen participants prior to randomization. Theoretical results show that retaining all compliers and screening out all non-compliers achieves three complementary aims: (i) the Local Average Treatment Effect is the same as the standard 2SLS estimator with no screening; (ii) median bias is minimized; and (iii) statistical power is maximized. In practice, complier status is unobserved.

title: An extragalactic gamma-ray binary formed in supernova 2022jli
creator: Pengfei Zhang 1,∗, Zhongxiang Wang 1,∗, Shunhao Ji 1
description: Abstract On May 5 2022, a type Ic supernova (SN) explosion SN 2022jli was discovered. This SN showed additional optical emissions, which were found to exhibit 12.4-day periodic undulations and concordant periodic velocity shifts. These key features likely indicate a compact object in a binary system was formed.

title: Transition rates and their applications in accelerated single-qubit for fermionic spinor field coupling
creator: Arnab Mukherjee ID *]Corresponding author, Sunandan Gangopadhyay ID, P. H. M. Barros ID, and H. A. S. Costa ID
description: Abstract In this work, we investigate the interaction between a uniformly accelerated single qubit and a fermionic spinor field. Here we consider both the massless and the massive fermionic spinor fields. The qubit-field interaction occurs over a finite time and was evolved via perturbation theory.

title: Primordial magnetic field from chiral plasma instability with sourcing
creator: Murman Gurgenidze, Andrew J. Long, Alberto Roper Pol, Axel Brandenburg, Tina Kahniashvili
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Murman Gurgenidze, Andrew J. Long, Alberto Roper Pol, Axel Brandenburg, Tina Kahniashvili. In an electron-positron plasma, an imbalance in the number of right- and left-chiral particles can lead to the growth of a helical magnetic field through a phenomenon called the chiral plasma instability (CPI). In the early universe, scattering reactions that violate chirality come into thermal equilibrium when the plasma cools below a temperature of approximately 80 ​ TeV 80\,\mathrm{TeV} .

title: Constructive Proofs of Generalized Boole–Fréchet Bounds: A Dynamic Programming Approach
creator: Kizito Salako
description: Abstract Extensions of the Boole–Fréchet inequalities give sharp bounds for the probabilities of compound events, particularly when only the probabilities of atomic events (that make up the compound events) are known. We present a constructive approach to obtaining generalized Boole–Fréchet bounds using dynamic programming.

title: Frequency- and phase-resolved polarimetry of millisecond pulsars and its application to timing 2015 Frequency- and phase-resolved polarimetry of millisecond pulsars and its application to timing – A.0.35
creator: Małgorzata Curyło, Andrew Zic, Shuangqiang Wang, Eric Thrane, Paul D. Lasky, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Zu-Cheng Chen, Shi Dai, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Agastya Kapur, Wenhua Ling, Marcus E. Lower, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Christopher J. Russell, Ryan M. Shannon, Xing-Jiang Zhu
description: Abstract Pulsar timing is used for a variety of applications including tests of fundamental physics, probing the structure of neutron stars, and detecting nanohertz gravitational waves. Development of robust methods and generation of high-quality timing data is therefore of utmost importance.

title: Bug Priority Change Prediction: An Exploratory Study on Apache Software Journal: TOSEM CCS: Software and its engineering Maintaining software
creator: Guangzong Cai, Zengyang Li, Peng Liang, Ran Mo, Hui Liu, Yutao Ma
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Guangzong Cai, Zengyang Li, Peng Liang, Ran Mo, Hui Liu, Yutao Ma. Bug fixing is a critical activity in the software development process. In issue tracking systems such as JIRA, each bug report is assigned a priority level to indicate the urgency and importance level of the bug. The priority may change during the bug fixing process, indicating that the urgency and importance level of the bug will change with the bug fixing.

title: Tracing a Multi-Temperature Quiescent Prominence’s Thermodynamic Evolution from Sun to Earth
creator: Callie A. García, Yeimy J. Rivera, Samuel T. Badman, John C. Raymond, Katharine K. Reeves, Tatiana Niembro, Kristoff W. Paulson, Michael L. Stevens
description: Abstract Solar prominences are cool, dense stable structures routinely observed in the corona. Prominences are often ejected from the Sun via coronal mass ejections (CMEs). However, they are rarely detected in a cool, low-ionized state within CMEs measured in situ, making their evolution hard to study.

title: Non-invasive Techniques for Flow Rate Measurement in Water Pipes: Protocol for a Systematic Review Thanks: This work was supported by the Universidad de Cuenca through the Vice-Rectorate for Research and Innovation under the project “Prediction of Water Consumption in Households Using Non-Invasive V
creator: Juan Diego Belesaca, Fabian Astudillo Salinas
description: Abstract Accurate, non-invasive flow measurement is imperative for efficient water resource management and leak detection in distribution systems. Despite the advent of diverse external sensing technologies, a paucity of consolidated evidence exists regarding their comparative performance, energy efficiency, and applicability in varied operational contexts.

title: Spontaneous Decoherence from Logarithmic Spectral Phase Deformations
creator: Sridhar Tayur
description: Abstract We examine a mechanism of spontaneous decoherence in which the generator of quantum dynamics is deformed to a logarithmically modified self-adjoint operator F β ​ ( H ) = H + β ​ H ​ log ⁡ H E ∗ F_{\beta}(H)=H+\beta H\log\frac{H}{E_{*}} for a positive self-adjoint Hamiltonian H H and a fixed reference scale E ∗ > 0 E_{*}>0

title: Beyond Algorithm Evolution: An LLM-Driven Framework for the Co-Evolution of Swarm Intelligence Optimization Algorithms and Prompts
creator: Shipeng Cen, Ying Tan
description: Abstract The field of automated algorithm design has been advanced by frameworks such as EoH, FunSearch, and Reevo. Yet, their focus on algorithm evolution alone, neglecting the prompts that guide them, limits their effectiveness with LLMs—especially in complex, uncertain environments where they nonetheless implicitly rely on strategies from swarm intelligence optimization algorithms.

title: OmniPSD: Layered PSD Generation with Diffusion Transformer
creator: Cheng Liu, Yiren Song, Haofan Wang, Mike Zheng Shou
description: Abstract Recent advances in diffusion models have greatly improved image generation and editing, yet generating or reconstructing layered PSD files with transparent alpha channels remains highly challenging. We propose OmniPSD, a unified diffusion framework built upon the Flux ecosystem that enables both text-to-PSD generation and image-to-PSD decomposition through in-context learning.

title: WTNN: Weibull-Tailored Neural Networks for survival analysis
creator: Gabrielle Rives, Nicolas Bousquet
description: Abstract The Weibull distribution is a commonly adopted choice for modeling the survival of systems subject to maintenance over time. When only proxy indicators and censored observations are available, it becomes necessary to express the distribution’s parameters as functions of time-dependent covariates.

title: Observation of ubiquitous charge correlations and hidden quantum critical point in hole-doped kagome superconductors
creator: Ilija K. Nikolov, Giuseppe Allodi, Adrien Rosuel, Ginevra Corsale, Anshu Kataria, Pietro Bonfà, Roberto De Renzi, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Marc-Henri Julien, Samuele Sanna, Vesna F. Mitrović
description: Abstract The interplay between superconductivity and charge-density wave (CDW) order, and its evolution with carrier density, is central to the physics of many quantum materials, notably high- T c T_{c} cuprates and kagome metals. Hole-doped kagome compounds exhibit puzzling double-dome superconductivity and, as chemical substitution inevitably introduces quenched disorder, their properties remain poorly understood.

title: Exploratory Mean-Variance with Jumps: An Equilibrium Approach
creator: Yuling Max Chen, Bin Li, David Saunders
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuling Max Chen, Bin Li, David Saunders. Revisiting the continuous-time Mean-Variance (MV) Portfolio Optimization problem, we model the market dynamics with a jump-diffusion process and apply Reinforcement Learning (RL) techniques to facilitate informed exploration within the control space. We recognize the time-inconsistency of the MV problem and adopt the time-inconsistent control (TIC) approach to analytically solve for an exploratory equilibrium investment policy, which is a Gaussian distribution centered on the equilibrium control of the classical MV problem.

title: L 1 L_{1} and L 2 L_{2} embeddings of the symmetric group
creator: Cosmas Kravaris
description: Abstract . We show that the Cayley graph of the symmetric group S ​ y ​ m n Sym_{n} generated by the cycle ( 123 ​ … ​ n ) (123...n) and the transposition ( 12 ) (12) embeds into L 1 L_{1} with bi-Lipschitz distortion O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) .

title: Understanding Xe isotopes near A = 130 A=130 through the prolate-oblate shape phase transition
creator: Wei Teng, Sheng-Nan Wang, Yu Zhang
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wei Teng, Sheng-Nan Wang, Yu Zhang. A simple algebraic scheme incorporating the prolate-oblate shape phase transition (SPT) is proposed within the framework of the interacting boson model to describe the quadrupole deformation features of Xe isotopes near A = 130 A=130 .

title: MelanomaNet: Explainable Deep Learning for Skin Lesion Classification
creator: Sukhrobbek Ilyosbekov
description: Abstract Automated skin lesion classification using deep learning has shown remarkable accuracy, yet clinical adoption remains limited due to the “black box” nature of these models. We present MelanomaNet, an explainable deep learning system for multi-class skin lesion classification that addresses this gap through four complementary interpretability mechanisms.

title: Goal Inference with Rao-Blackwellized Particle Filters Thanks: This research was supported in part by Air Force Office of Scientific Research award number FA9550-22-1-0429. Any opinions, findings and conclusions or recommendations expressed in this material are those of the author(s) and do not nece
creator: Yixuan Wang, Dan P. Guralnik, Warren E Dixon
description: Abstract Inferring the eventual goal of a mobile agent from noisy observations of its trajectory is a fundamental estimation problem. We initiate the study of such intent inference using a variant of a Rao–Blackwellized Particle Filter (RBPF), subject to the assumption that the agent’s intent manifests through closed-loop behavior with a state-of-the-art provable practical stability property.

title: Efficient MoE Serving in the Memory-Bound Regime: Balance Activated Experts, Not Tokens
creator: Yanpeng Yu, Haiyue Ma, Krish Agarwal, Nicolai Oswald, Qijing Huang, Hugo Linsenmaier, Chunhui Mei, Ritchie Zhao, Ritika Borkar, Bita Darvish Rouhani, David Nellans, Ronny Krashinsky, Anurag Khandelwal
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yanpeng Yu, Haiyue Ma, Krish Agarwal, Nicolai Oswald, Qijing Huang, Hugo Linsenmaier, Chunhui Mei, Ritchie Zhao, Ritika Borkar, Bita Darvish Rouhani, David Nellans, Ronny Krashinsky, Anurag Khandelwal. Expert Parallelism (EP) permits Mixture of Experts (MoE) models to scale beyond a single GPU. To address load imbalance across GPUs in EP, existing approaches aim to balance the number of tokens each GPU processes.

title: Embedding 𝗄 \mathsf{k} -algebras into Leavitt algebra L 𝗄 ​ ( 1 , 2 ) L_{\mathsf{k}}(1,2)
creator: Boris Bilich, Roozbeh Hazrat, Tran Giang Nam
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Boris Bilich, Roozbeh Hazrat, Tran Giang Nam. Since the commutative monoid T = ( { 0 , 1 } , ∨ ) T=(\{0,1\},\vee) is a weak terminal object in the category of conical monoids with order units, there is a unital homomorphism from every Bergman 𝗄 \mathsf{k} -algebra corresponding to a conical finitely generated commutative monoid into the Leavitt algebra L 𝗄 ​ ( 1 , 2 ) L_{\mathsf{k}}(1,2) , where 𝗄 \mathsf{k} is a field.

title: Anomalous collective modes in atomic nuclei within the proton-neutron interacting boson model
creator: Wei Teng, Yu Zhang, Sheng-Nan Wang, Feng Pan, Chong Qi, J. P. Draayer
description: Abstract Novel collective modes characterized by a B 4 / 2 B_{4/2} ratio ( ≡ B ( E 2 ; 4 1 + → 2 1 + ) / B ( E 2 ; 2 1 + → 0 1 + ) \equiv B(E2;4_{1}^{+}\rightarrow 2_{1}^{+})/B(E2;2_{1}^{+}\rightarrow 0_{1}^{+}) ) less than 1.

title: A Modular Lean 4 Framework for Confluence and Strong Normalization of Lambda Calculi with Products and Sums
creator: Arthur F. Ramos, Anjolina G. de Oliveira, Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz, Tiago M. L. de Veras
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arthur F. Ramos, Anjolina G. de Oliveira, Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz, Tiago M. L. de Veras. We present Metatheory , a comprehensive library for programming language foundations in Lean 4, featuring a modular framework for proving confluence of abstract rewriting systems.

title: Analysis of the Security Design, Engineering, and Implementation of the SecureDNA System PubID: pubid: Network and Distributed System Security (NDSS) Symposium 2026 23-27 February 2026, San Diego, CA, USA ISBN XXX-X-XXXXXXX-X-X https://dx.doi.org/10.14722/ndss.2026.[23 | | 24]xxxx www.ndss-symposium
creator: Alan T. Sherman, Jeremy J. Romanik Romano, Edward Zieglar, Enis Golaszewski, Jonathan D. Fuchs, William E. Byrd
description: Abstract We analyze security aspects of the SecureDNA system regarding its system design, engineering, and implementation. This system enables DNA synthesizers to screen order requests against a database of hazards. By applying novel cryptography involving distributed oblivious pseudorandom functions, the system aims to keep order requests and the database of hazards secret.

title: SITP: A High-Reliability Semantic Information Transport Protocol Without Retransmission for Semantic Communication Thanks: This work was supported in part by the National Science and Technology Major Project-Mobile Information Networks under Grant No.2024ZD1300700, and in part by the Natural Science
creator: Yunhao Wang, Shuai Ma
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yunhao Wang, Shuai Ma. With the evolution of 6G networks, modern communication systems are facing unprecedented demands for high reliability and low latency. However, conventional transport protocols are designed for bit-level reliability, failing to meet the semantic robustness requirements. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel Semantic Information Transport Protocol (SITP), which achieves TCP-level reliability and UDP-level latency by verifying only packet headers while retaining potentially corrupted payloads for semantic decoding.

title: The ONs and OFFs of Pulsar Radio Emission: Characterizing the Nulling Phenomenon
creator: Garvit Grover, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Samuel J. McSweeney, Christopher P. Lee, Chia Min Tan, Shih Ching Fu, Bradley W. Meyers
description: Abstract Radio emission from pulsars is known to exhibit a diverse range of emission phenomena, among which nulling, where the emission becomes temporarily undetectable, is an intriguing one. Observations suggest nulling is prevalent in many long-period pulsars and must be understood to obtain a more comprehensive picture of pulsar emission and its evolution.

title: A physics-augmented neural network framework for modeling and detecting thermo-visco-plastic behavior
creator: Reese E. Jones, Asghar Jadoon, D. Thomas Seidl, Jan N. Fuhg
description: Abstract Although considerable attention has been devoted to the development of models for isothermal, rate-independent plasticity, many high-consequence performance assessments involve viscoplastic processes that generate substantial heat. In addition, materials may transit from a nearly isothermal, rate-independent regime to a viscous, temperature-dependent regime during these processes, which makes modeling more challenging.

title: A Benamou–Brenier proximal splitting method for constrained unbalanced optimal transport
creator: Mao Nishino, Martin Bauer, Tom Needham, Nicolas Charon
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mao Nishino, Martin Bauer, Tom Needham, Nicolas Charon. The dynamic formulation of optimal transport, also known as the Benamou-Brenier formulation, has been extended to the unbalanced case by introducing a source term in the continuity equation. When this source term is penalized based on the Fisher-Rao metric, the resulting model is referred to as the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) setting, and allows for the comparison between any two positive measures without the need for equalized total mass.

title: Vaccine sieve analysis on deep sequencing data using competing risks Cox regression with failure type subject to misclassification
creator: James Peng, Michal Juraska, Pamela A. Shaw, Peter B. Gilbert
description: Abstract Understanding how vaccines perform against different pathogen genotypes is crucial for developing effective prevention strategies, particularly for highly genetically diverse pathogens like HIV. Sieve analysis is a statistical framework used to determine whether a vaccine selectively prevents acquisition of certain genotypes while allowing breakthrough of other genotypes that evade immune responses.

title: On the Green’s functions and Martin boundary structure of a planar diffusion in a discontinuous layered medium Thanks: This project has received funding from Agence Nationale de la Recherche, ANR JCJC programme under the Grant Agreement ANR-22-CE40-0002 (ANR RESYST).
creator: Sandro Franceschi, Irina Kourkova, Maxence Petit
description: Abstract . We consider a two-dimensional diffusion process in a two-layered plane, governed by distinct covariance matrices in the upper and lower half-planes and by two drift vectors pointed away from the x x -axis. We first analyze the case where the generator of the process is in divergence form, that is, when the flux is continuous across the interface.
